statement: By the time a05 ran, crates/enforcer-domain/src/hashes.rs already fully defined a branded Sha256 newtype (private inner String, parse-at-boundary TryFrom<String>/FromStr rejecting missing sha256: prefix / wrong length / uppercase / non-hex, serde try_from/into wiring, Debug/Clone/PartialEq/Eq/Hash/PartialOrd/Ord/Display/ts_rs::TS derives) and was already consumed by crates/enforcer-scan/src/rules/baseline_ratchet.rs (BaselineEntry-set integrity hash) and crates/enforcer-proof/src/envelope.rs (proof-entry integrity hash) via enforcer_domain::hashes::Sha256. The one Requirement Checklist item missing was a direct hashing constructor: every existing consumer minted a Sha256 by calling enforcer_core::hash_chain::link_digest(None, bytes) (a hash-CHAIN primitive, not a plain-hash API) and then .parse::<Sha256>(), instead of calling a Sha256::of(bytes) constructor as the workpack specifies.
why: The a05 workpack's owns line (crates/enforcer-domain/src/sha256.rs) and prose read as if the Sha256 newtype did not exist yet, but a02-adjacent/arc-02 work had already landed it in hashes.rs under a different filename, with the SAME prefixed wire form (sha256:<64 lowercase hex>) the workpack's parse-at-boundary regex describes minus the sha256: prefix literal. Renaming the module or changing the wire form would have broken both existing consumers (baseline_ratchet.rs, envelope.rs).
howToApply: Before creating a workpack's named 'owns' file, grep the crate for the type name the workpack is about to define; if it already exists under a different filename and is already consumed by dependent crates with a specific wire form, EXTEND the existing file in place (add only the missing constructor/method) rather than creating the named file or changing the established wire form -- this is the same pattern a04 (paths.rs vs path.rs) and a06 (ids.rs vs coordination_ids.rs) already documented.

statement: Extended crates/enforcer-domain/src/hashes.rs in place (no new file) with: a Sha256::of(bytes: &[u8]) -> Sha256 hashing constructor that hashes directly via sha2::Sha256 (added sha2 = { workspace = true } to enforcer-domain's own Cargo.toml -- sha2 was already a [workspace.dependencies] entry via enforcer-core, so this is a leaf-crate dependency addition, not a root-manifest edit) rather than delegating to enforcer_core::hash_chain::link_digest, to avoid coupling a plain-hash API to a hash-CHAIN primitive's semantics; a sha256_brand_decode test matching TEST_PROOF_EXPECTATIONS.md row a05's named oracle, covering of()+parse() round-trip, determinism, the well-known empty-input digest, and length/case/charset rejection via both FromStr/TryFrom and the serde boundary; and a compile-reject fixture documented as a code comment (proved at review time, consistent with a04/a06's no-trybuild convention) since Sha256's only field is private with no From<String> impl.
why: TEST_PROOF_EXPECTATIONS.md row a05 (PENDING at start of this lane) names 'sha256-brand-decode round-trip + compile-reject fixture' as the required proof; the newtype's validation/derives/consumers already satisfied every other Requirement Checklist item, so the only functional gap was the missing of() constructor plus the named-proof-row test coverage.
howToApply: For any future ax0 workpack whose target type already exists under a different filename with an established wire form already consumed by other crates, follow this lane's approach: add only the missing method(s), reuse an already-workspace-declared dependency rather than introducing a new crypto/parsing dependency, and write the TEST_PROOF_EXPECTATIONS-named test in the existing module's #[cfg(test)] block.
